script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for April 18. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

London taxi drivers spend years memorizing 25,000 streets—and their brains physically grow larger in the hippocampus, the navigation center.  Meanwhile, studies suggest GPS users may be losing spatial memory.  Navigation is a skill that grows or shrinks with use.

London's famous 'Knowledge' test requires taxi drivers to memorize thousands of routes. Brain scans show their hippocampi—the memory-and-navigation regions—are significantly larger than average. Navigation literally grows the brain. Research suggests heavy GPS reliance correlates with reduced hippocampal activity and worse spatial memory.  We navigate successfully but build no mental map.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Skills atrophy without practice.  Navigation teaches that convenience can cost capability.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Wayfinding Exercise - Build Your Mental Map.

Here's your activity: Navigate somewhere familiar without GPS today. Pay attention to landmarks, turns, and distances. Try to build a mental map as you go. Afterward, could you give directions? Regular practice keeps this skill sharp. This helps you actively practice spatial memory.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about finding your way can be applied to wayfinding exercise - build your mental map. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
